speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or changes in your stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus.

The history of bilious vomiting in a newborn six hours after birth is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. Given the family history of pyloric stenosis, we must rule out other causes, but the bilious nature of the vomit strongly suggests midgut obstruction. I will now request an abdominal ultrasound to evaluate for malrotation and volvulus. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound images.
